prompt_text: I need a personal injury lawyer in Columbus after a car accident. Which specific law firms should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Columbus Ohio for a car accident case?
answer_verbatim:
I can do that — but to give the best, specific firm recommendations I need two quick things from you:
- Which part of Columbus (ZIP or neighborhood) so I can focus on local firms, and
- A short summary of the accident/injury (any serious injuries, whether you were partially at fault, and whether the other driver had insurance).

If you want names right away, I can’t safely invent or guess firms’ current offices or specialties without checking — but I can immediately tell you exactly where to find reputable Columbus personal-injury lawyers and what specific firms or sources to call, plus what to ask them and what documents to have ready. That will get you good, reliable options fast.

Below is an immediate action plan you can use right now, and the key questions to ask when you call any firm.

Immediate places to find reputable Columbus personal-injury lawyers
- Columbus Bar Association Lawyer Referral Service — they can refer you to local attorneys who handle car-accident injury cases.
- Ohio State Bar Association referral or online directory — statewide listings and certified specialists.
- Super Lawyers (Ohio/Columbus listings) — identifies attorneys rated by peer review and independent research.
- Avvo and Martindale-Hubbell — client reviews, peer ratings, and discipline history.
- Local hospital/clinic social work or victim services — they often keep lists of experienced personal-injury attorneys.

What types of firms to call
- Contingency-fee personal injury firms (they advance costs and get paid only if you recover).
- Small trial boutiques that handle serious injury and wrongful-death cases (good if your case may go to trial).
- Larger national plaintiffs’ firms with a Columbus office (may have more resources for complex cases).

What to ask on your first call (keep it short — aim for 10–15 minutes)
1. Do you handle car-accident personal injury cases in Columbus? (If yes:) Do you take them on contingency? What is your contingency fee percentage and what costs would I be responsible for if we don’t win?
2. How many car-accident cases have you handled that went to trial? (If serious injury or disputed fault, prefer a trial-experienced lawyer.)
3. Have you handled cases like mine (describe injuries/issue briefly)? What was a typical outcome?
4. Who will handle my case day-to-day (attorney or paralegal)? Will I ever pay to get documents or medical records up front?
5. What is your typical timeline for resolving cases like mine?
6. Can you give references or recent verdicts/settlements in Columbus?

Documents and information to have ready for the call
- Date/time/location of the crash and a brief timeline of events
- Photos of damage and injuries, if you have them
- Any police report number and officer name/precinct
- Insurance information (your insurer and other driver’s)
- Medical treatment summary (where treated, current doctors)
- Names/contact of witnesses (if known)

Red flags to avoid
- Firms that pressure you to sign immediately without answering questions
- Lawyers who won’t provide a clear fee agreement or who give vague answers about costs
- Lowball guarantees (“we’ll get you X dollars”) — outcome depends on facts

If you want, give your ZIP and 2–3 sentence summary of the accident/injuries and I’ll list 5 specific Columbus personal-injury firms you should call first (with short reasons for each pick and what to expect from them). I can also draft a short phone script you can use on those calls. Which would you prefer?
